title: My Morning
text: I get up at six o'clock every day. It is still dark outside. I wash my face and brush my teeth, and then I make coffee.
My wife gets up later. She does not like mornings. She drinks tea, not coffee. We eat breakfast together at half past six. We usually have bread and eggs.
At seven o'clock I leave the house. The street is already busy. Many people are going to work, and the children are going to school.
I like the morning because it is quiet inside my head. Nobody calls me. Nobody needs me. I have thirty minutes for myself, and that is enough.

questions.q: What time does the writer get up?
questions.explainVi: Câu đầu tiên: "I get up at six o'clock every day." Nửa sáu (half past six) là giờ ăn sáng, bảy giờ là giờ ra khỏi nhà.

questions.q: What does his wife drink?
questions.explainVi: "She drinks tea, not coffee." Chú ý cấu trúc "A, not B" — cách nói phủ định rất hay gặp trong hội thoại.

questions.q: Why does he like the morning?
options: Because he has time for himself
questions.explainVi: "I have thirty minutes for myself, and that is enough." Cà phê và phố đông chỉ là chi tiết, không phải lý do.

title: At the Coffee Shop
text: "Good morning. What can I get you?"
"Hi. Can I have an iced coffee, please?"
"Sure. Small, medium, or large?"
"Medium, please. And not too sweet."
"No problem. Anything else?"
"Yes, one sandwich. How much is it?"
"That's ninety thousand dong. Is it for here or to go?"
"To go, please. Here you are."
"Thank you. Your name, please?"
"Minh. M-I-N-H."
"Thanks, Minh. It will be ready in three minutes."

glossary.vi: dùng tại chỗ hay mang đi

questions.q: What size does Minh order?
questions.explainVi: "Medium, please." Ba cỡ chuẩn ở mọi quán: small – medium – large.

questions.q: Does Minh eat in the shop?
questions.explainVi: "To go, please." — mang đi. Nếu ăn tại chỗ thì trả lời "For here."

questions.q: How long will Minh wait?
questions.explainVi: Câu cuối: "It will be ready in three minutes." Chú ý đừng lẫn với "ninety thousand" — đó là số tiền, không phải thời gian.

title: My Small Room
text: I live in a small room in District 3. It is not big, but it is enough for one person.
There is a bed near the window. There is a desk next to the bed, and my computer is on the desk. There are two chairs, but I only use one. The other chair has my clothes on it.
There is no kitchen in my room. I cook with a small pot on the floor. It is not comfortable, but it is cheap.
The best thing is the window. In the afternoon the sun comes in, and the whole room turns orange. I sit on the bed and I do nothing. Those ten minutes are my favourite part of the day.

questions.q: Where is the desk?
questions.explainVi: "There is a desk next to the bed." Cái ở gần cửa sổ là chiếc giường.

questions.q: How many chairs does he use?
questions.explainVi: "There are two chairs, but I only use one." Chiếc còn lại dùng để vắt quần áo.

questions.q: What does he like most about the room?
questions.explainVi: "The best thing is the window." Rẻ là một ưu điểm, nhưng "best thing" mới là câu trả lời.

title: Getting to Work
text: It takes me about forty minutes to get to work. I could take the bus, but I ride my motorbike because it is faster — most of the time.

Last Monday it rained very hard. I stopped under a bridge with about twenty other people. We all waited there for fifteen minutes and nobody said anything. Then the rain stopped and everybody drove away at the same time.
I was thirty minutes late. My manager looked at me and said, "Rain again?" I said yes. He laughed and said, "Buy a raincoat that actually works."
Now I keep a raincoat under my seat. I have not used it yet, but I feel better knowing it is there.

glossary.vi: vẫn chưa (dùng ở câu phủ định)

questions.q: Why does he ride a motorbike instead of taking the bus?
questions.explainVi: "because it is faster — most of the time." Cụm "most of the time" (phần lớn thời gian) là lời cảnh báo trước cho chuyện mưa ở đoạn sau.

questions.q: How did the manager react?
questions.explainVi: "He laughed and said…" — sếp cười và đùa về chiếc áo mưa, không hề tức giận.

questions.q: Has he used the new raincoat?
questions.explainVi: "I have not used it yet." Đây là hiện tại hoàn thành + "yet" — chuyện chưa xảy ra tính đến bây giờ.

title: A Message from My Boss
text: Hi Lan,
Quick update before tomorrow. The client moved our meeting from 2 p.m. to 10 a.m., so we have less time than I hoped.
Could you please send me the sales numbers for June and July before you leave today? I do not need the full report — just the two totals and anything strange you noticed.
If you cannot finish it today, that is fine. Let me know and I will ask Trung instead. Please do not stay late for this.
Thanks a lot,
David

glossary.vi: Bạn giúp mình… được không? (lịch sự)

questions.q: What changed about the meeting?
questions.explainVi: "moved our meeting from 2 p.m. to 10 a.m." — động từ "move" ở đây nghĩa là dời lịch, không phải di chuyển.

questions.q: What exactly does David want?
questions.explainVi: "I do not need the full report — just the two totals and anything strange you noticed."

questions.q: What should Lan do if she runs out of time?
options: Tell him so he can ask Trung
questions.explainVi: "Let me know and I will ask Trung instead. Please do not stay late for this." Câu này là mẫu rất hay dùng khi từ chối việc mà vẫn lịch sự.

title: Shopping Before Tet
text: Two days before Tet, the market is the busiest place in the city. My mother goes at five in the morning to get the best flowers.

This year she took me with her. "Watch and learn," she said. She picked up a branch of yellow apricot blossom and asked the price. The seller said eight hundred thousand. My mother put it down and started walking away. The seller called after her: six hundred.
"Never buy the first price," my mother told me later. "And never look happy."
We came home with flowers, three kilos of oranges, and a chicken. I carried everything. My mother carried nothing and looked very pleased with herself.
I think she was right about the price. I am still not sure about the part where I carry everything.

questions.q: How did the mother get a lower price?
questions.explainVi: "My mother put it down and started walking away." Bỏ đi là chiêu mặc cả — người bán gọi với theo và hạ giá.

questions.q: How much did the flowers finally cost?
questions.explainVi: Người bán gọi với theo "six hundred" — tức 600 nghìn, và họ mang hoa về nhà.

questions.q: What is the tone at the end?
questions.explainVi: "I am still not sure about the part where I carry everything" — cách nói đùa nhẹ, kiểu than phiền vui vẻ.

title: The Job Interview
text: I arrived twenty minutes early, which meant I had twenty minutes to be nervous in the lobby.

The interviewer was younger than I expected. She started with the usual question: "Tell me about yourself." I had practised that answer forty times, so it came out smoothly. Then she asked something I had not prepared for: "What is something you are bad at?"

I thought about lying. Instead I told the truth. I said I was slow at making decisions because I always want more information first. Then I explained what I had changed: I now give myself a deadline and decide even when the picture is not complete.
She wrote something down and nodded. "Good," she said. "Most people say they work too hard."
I got the job. I still think the honest answer was the reason. People can tell when you are reading from a script, and nobody trusts a person with no weaknesses.

questions.q: Which question was he not ready for?
options: Why do you want this job?
questions.explainVi: "Then she asked something I had not prepared for: 'What is something you are bad at?'" Câu đầu thì anh đã luyện 40 lần.

questions.q: What did he do about his weakness?
questions.explainVi: "I now give myself a deadline and decide even when the picture is not complete." Công thức trả lời điểm yếu: nói thật + nói cách đang khắc phục.

questions.q: Why does he think honesty worked?
questions.explainVi: "People can tell when you are reading from a script, and nobody trusts a person with no weaknesses."

title: Booking a Hotel in Da Nang
titleVi: Đặt khách sạn ở Đà Nẵng
text: "Good afternoon, Blue Sea Hotel. How may I help you?"
"Hello. I'd like to book a room for three nights, from the 14th to the 17th."
"Certainly. How many guests?"
"Two adults and one child. She's six."
"We have a deluxe room with a sea view at 1.4 million a night, or a standard room at 950,000. Children under seven stay free."
"Does the price include breakfast?"
"Yes, breakfast for two is included. Would you like the sea view?"
"Let me think. Is the standard room quiet?"
"It faces the road, so it can be noisy in the morning."
"Then I'll take the deluxe. Can I pay when I arrive?"
"Of course. Could I have your full name and phone number, please?"

glossary.vi: Để tôi nghĩ đã (câu câu giờ rất hữu ích)

questions.q: How much does the family pay per night?
questions.explainVi: Cuối cùng khách chọn deluxe: "Then I'll take the deluxe" — 1,4 triệu/đêm. Bé 6 tuổi miễn phí.

questions.q: Why does he avoid the standard room?
questions.explainVi: "It faces the road, so it can be noisy in the morning." Phòng standard rẻ hơn, nhưng ồn.

questions.q: When will he pay?
questions.explainVi: "Can I pay when I arrive?" — "Of course." Cách hỏi này rất hay dùng khi đặt phòng qua điện thoại.

title: Why I Started Running
titleVi: Vì sao tôi bắt đầu chạy bộ
text: For years I told myself I would start exercising "next month". Next month kept arriving and I kept not running.
What finally worked was making the goal embarrassingly small. My rule was simple: put on my shoes and go outside. That was the whole goal. I did not have to run. I only had to stand on the street.

Of course, once you are outside in running shoes, you feel silly going back in. So you run a little. Some days I ran four kilometres. Some days I ran two hundred metres and came home. Both counted as success, because the goal was never the distance.

That was fourteen months ago. I have missed plenty of days, and I stopped completely for three weeks when I got sick. But I always came back, because coming back to "put on your shoes" is much easier than coming back to "run five kilometres".
The habit was never about running. It was about making the first step so small that my lazy brain could not argue with it.

glossary.vi: đến mức ngại (ở đây: nhỏ đến mức buồn cười)

questions.q: What was his actual daily goal?
options: To put on shoes and go outside
questions.explainVi: "My rule was simple: put on my shoes and go outside. That was the whole goal."

questions.q: How did he treat a 200-metre day?
questions.explainVi: "Both counted as success, because the goal was never the distance."

questions.q: What is the main lesson?
questions.explainVi: Câu cuối: "making the first step so small that my lazy brain could not argue with it". Anh ấy còn thừa nhận đã nghỉ 3 tuần — nên đáp án "không bao giờ nghỉ" là sai.
